title: OS command execution via Process.Start (csharp) — review required
description: The csharp sink Process.Start hands its argument to a command shell or process launcher. If any part of the argument derives from untrusted input, an attacker can inject extra commands. This lexical rule flags the sink; the reviewer confirms every argument is trusted or safely separated from the command.
remediation: Avoid the sink: use argument-vector APIs (ProcessStartInfo with ArgumentList) so untrusted data never passes through a shell. If a shell is unavoidable, pin an allowlist of commands and quote every interpolated value.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any Process.Start call matches, including fully trusted invocations. Dataflow from untrusted input is not proven — treat every hit as review-required.
